title: Elective Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Preparation

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults having primary elective hip or knee replacement: shared decisions, prehabilitation, major-surgery tests, tranexamic acid, VTE prophylaxis and antibiotic prophylaxis. Verified against NICE NG157 (joint replacement), NG45, NG89 and Saudi MOH Protocol-015 (orthopaedic prophylaxis, MRSA screening).
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: IV tranexamic acid dose (NICE refers to the SmPC)
SFDA registration not checked per drug
Local antibiogram may add gentamicin (MOH p. 1)

pathophysiology.summary: Joint replacement relieves pain and restores function in end-stage joint disease (usually osteoarthritis) by replacing worn articular surfaces with an implant. Main risks are bleeding, VTE, infection of the prosthesis and dislocation.
keyMechanisms: Cartilage loss and bone remodelling cause pain and stiffness that fail non-surgical care.
Major lower-limb surgery and immobility raise VTE risk — prophylaxis for 14–38 days (NICE NG89).
Implant infection is hard to treat — MRSA screening, prophylaxis and ultra-clean air (MOH, NICE).
Tranexamic acid reduces blood loss (NICE NG157).

symptoms: Joint pain limiting walking, sleep and daily activities despite non-surgical treatment.
physicalSigns: Reduced range of movement, deformity, antalgic gait.
Skin condition over the joint; distal pulses.
redFlags: Active infection anywhere (skin, urine, teeth) — defer surgery
Calf swelling or breathlessness after surgery — VTE

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Decolonise with nasal mupirocin and chlorhexidine body wash for 5 days; vancomycin alternative prophylaxis (MOH p. 2).

clinicalManagement.title: Shared decision and prehabilitation
actions: Discuss alternatives, benefits, risks, implant options and anaesthesia (NICE NG157).
Prehabilitation advice: exercises, weight, diet, smoking cessation (NICE NG157 1.2).
Offer regional or general anaesthesia with local infiltration analgesia (NICE NG157 1.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Blood conservation
actions: Give IV tranexamic acid; if no renal impairment also 1–2 g topical intra-articular before closure; total combined dose not above 3 g (NICE NG157 1.4).
Use 2 implant 'stop moments' and ultra-clean air theatres (NICE NG157).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Hip: LMWH 10 days then aspirin 75 or 150 mg for 28 days; or LMWH 28 days with stockings; or rivaroxaban (NICE NG89 1.11.5).
Knee: aspirin 75 or 150 mg for 14 days; or LMWH 14 days with stockings; or rivaroxaban (NICE NG89 1.11.8).
Enoxaparin label dose for hip/knee replacement: 30 mg SC every 12 h (hip alternative 40 mg once daily).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: Total joint replacement: cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min of incision (MOH p. 2).
Allergy or MRSA: clindamycin 900 mg (60 min) or vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 2 g) within 120 min (MOH p. 2).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).

learningObjectives: Prepare adults for primary hip or knee replacement with evidence-based blood, infection and VTE measures.

keyPoints: Major surgery: FBC, renal function and ECG for most.
Tranexamic acid, total not above 3 g.
Cefazolin 2 g; screen and decolonise MRSA.
pitfalls: Topical tranexamic acid in renal impairment.

patientEducation: Exercises before and after surgery; recovery expectations; when to return to driving and work (NICE NG157).
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking and reduce alcohol before surgery (NICE NG180).
Stay active; prehabilitation exercises where advised.
dischargeCriteria: Pain controlled with oral analgesia; eating, drinking and mobilising.
Wound satisfactory; VTE prophylaxis plan and follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Post-operative review per surgical team; return immediately with fever, wound redness, calf swelling, breathlessness or chest pain.
